children: Elon Musk is not known for underselling timelines, but his latest prediction for SpaceX's AI ambitions is striking even by his standards. On September 24, Musk said SpaceX could have a model comparable to Anthropic's Fable or OpenAI's GPT-6 ready within two to three months.

The AI push at SpaceX is not purely theoretical. The company has already reassigned a few dozen engineers from its Starlink and Starship programs specifically to work on AI development, a meaningful signal of internal prioritization given how resource-constrained those flagship programs tend to be.

SpaceX's AI work builds on the Grok family of models developed under xAI. Grok 4.5, which launched in June 2026, runs on a 1.5 trillion-parameter base model and entered private beta at SpaceX and Tesla shortly after launch. The model also incorporates data from Cursor, the AI coding tool.

Speaking of Cursor: SpaceX acquired the startup, with reported deal values ranging between $6 billion and $60 billion in stock. Musk also outlined an aggressive release cadence. SpaceX intends to ship new foundation models every month through the rest of 2026.
Musk went further than the two-to-three month window. He projected that if SpaceX maintains its current growth trajectory, the company could take a leading position in AI within six months.

The monthly release strategy is perhaps the most consequential detail. If SpaceX follows through, it introduces a new kind of competitive pressure: not just better models, but faster model improvement cycles.

There is also a talent dimension worth tracking. SpaceX pulling engineers from Starlink and Starship is not cost-free. Both programs have their own ambitious timelines, and the reallocation creates a resource tension that will only grow if the AI push intensifies.

title: Elon Musk says SpaceX could have a Fable or GPT-6 level AI model within months
